rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst, noting cohesive ICM, reasonable TE, intact zona, and possible handling-related collapse. However, it introduces uncertainty and some speculative features (debris, dust, discrepancy with grading) and is not fully precise about stage.

Integrates age, BMI, AMH/FSH, tubal factor, sperm parameters, endometrial thickness, and first-cycle status well, and appropriately highlights hydrosalpinx as a key modifier. Could more explicitly connect some factors to embryo competence versus uterine receptivity.

Overall logic is understandable, but there are internal inconsistencies: repeated uncertainty about stage 3 vs expanded blastocyst, mixed probability statements, and some overreach in estimating euploidy/live birth from morphology alone.

Mostly aligned with IVF practice: supports single embryo transfer, cautions against overusing add-ons in a first cycle, and appropriately flags untreated hydrosalpinx. Minor deviations include somewhat optimistic outcome estimates and loose handling of Gardner stage terminology.

Provides practical next steps including proceeding with single embryo transfer, confirming hydrosalpinx treatment, ensuring luteal support, standard post-transfer care, and restrained future-cycle escalation. Useful and clinically relevant, though not highly detailed on protocol specifics.
